part: What it cost, and the close
html:
Where to Go From Here

One Behavior

Scenario, the right red, code, green, gated commit. Held by hooks while nobody watches.

Generic Components

ARTIE, the gateway, heart-mcp, Buster: built the same way.

One Media Type

Five services, one kept script, one generic client.

Try the bdd-gates skill on your own repository: Kotlin with Gradle, TypeScript with Node, C# with .NET.

bdd-gates skill · heart-rise-artie · reports
say: Recall the question I started with: have you ever asked an agent to do the same thing twice and gotten two different answers? Here's what I did about it. In the middle, one behavior at a time: a scenario first, a red run that fails for the right reason, the code, a green run, a gated commit, held by hooks while I was out walking the dog and dictating into my phone. Around that, generic components built the same way. And around those, a release across five services that share nothing but a media type, driven by one script that a model found once and nobody needs to pay for again. The bdd-gates skill is public. So is everything you saw, and the reports behind it. Try the skill on your own repository; it supports Kotlin with Gradle, TypeScript with Node, and C# with .NET today. And if your agents keep giving you two different answers, come and find me.
